transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today. I really appreciate it, and I hope I'm not wasting your time. I know you must be very busy with people who have much bigger problems. 

But, well, I guess what brings me in is that I've just sort of... stopped wanting to do the things that usually keep me going. It's probably just a silly rut, and I should just push through it, right? But lately I haven't been going to my salsa nights or the church gatherings. I usually love cooking for the neighbors, and I just haven't had it in me to do that either. I haven't even wanted to walk into my carpentry shop just to enjoy the smell of the wood, which is usually my favorite part of the day. 

Does that make sense? I just wanted to make sure I was doing the right thing by coming in to ask about it.
How long have you been feeling this way, and has it been happening every day?

Well, let's see... I'd say it's been about two months now. It sort of started when my wife's health took a sudden turn for the worse. We had to change our whole routine, and I guess I just haven't adjusted very well. I know I should be stronger for her, and I'm really trying not to let it get to me every single day, but... yeah, it's pretty much been a daily struggle since then. I hope it's okay that I'm bringing this up, I just want to make sure I'm doing everything I can to get back on track for her sake. Am I explaining that alright?
Do you find that most days you feel down, sad, or hopeless, even when there's no specific reason for it?

Well... I wouldn't want to use a strong word like hopeless, because I know I have so much to be grateful for, and I really don't want to sound like I'm just complaining. But... I guess, yes, I do feel pretty down. 

Most mornings I wake up with this... I don't know, this heavy, just sort of empty feeling right in my chest. It's hard to explain, but it’s almost like the color has just completely gone out of the house, if that makes sense? 

I feel terrible even admitting that out loud. I actually have to force myself not to break down and cry, especially in front of my wife. She has enough on her plate with her health, and she needs me to be strong right now. I really don't want to burden her with me being overly emotional. I shouldn't be getting so tearful over nothing, right? I hope it's okay that I'm telling you all this... I just want to make sure I'm answering your question the way you need me to.
Have you noticed that you no longer enjoy activities that used to bring you pleasure, like your carpentry or spending time with friends at church?

Well, yes... I know I mentioned that a little bit when I first sat down, and I hope I'm not repeating myself too much. I just... I really want to be helpful and give you the right information. 

But yes, it's exactly that. I used to really look forward to those things. The salsa nights, seeing everyone at the church gatherings, even just cooking a little something for the neighbors... it all just feels like so much effort now. And my carpentry shop... that's probably the hardest part to admit. I used to just go out there and breathe in the sawdust and the pine, and it would make my whole day. Now I just... I look at the door and I can't even bring myself to turn the handle. 

I know it probably sounds incredibly lazy of me, and I really should just force myself to go out there and be productive. It's just a phase, right? I'm sure if I just try harder, I can get back to enjoying it. Does that sound like the right way to handle it?
Have you been feeling like you’re a failure or that you’re letting others down, even when there’s no real reason to think that?

Well... I don't want to sound like I'm throwing a pity party, because I know I'm doing my best. But... yes, I suppose I do feel that way sometimes. 

It's just... I keep replaying everything in my head. Every doctor's appointment we went to, every little change in her health before things got bad. I can't help but tell myself that... well, that a better husband would have caught it sooner, you know? Like I should have noticed something was wrong, or... or protected her somehow. 

I know it's probably silly to think that way, and I really try not to dwell on it because it doesn't do her any good. I'm probably just overthinking things, right? I just... I feel like I let her down when she needed me most. I hope it's alright that I'm sharing that with you, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the whole picture. Am I giving you the kind of information you need?
Have you noticed that you’ve been feeling much more tired or that you’ve lost a lot of your energy lately, even when you’re not doing anything physically demanding?

Well... I hate to admit it, because I know I shouldn't be complaining about being tired when I'm not even working out in the shop right now. I feel like I should have all the energy in the world. But... yes, I have been feeling pretty worn out. 

It's strange, really. Even if I've just been sitting down, or... or even after getting a full night in bed, my body just feels so heavy. It's like... well, it feels like I've been framing a roof all day in the sun, even when I haven't done much of anything. Just doing small chores, like... like trying to load a few tools into the truck, it just feels like it's entirely too much effort. 

I know I just need to push through it and stop being so sluggish. I'm sure it's just my body adjusting to not working as much, right? I really hope I don't sound like I'm just making excuses to be lazy. Is it normal to feel this drained when you're just... sitting around? I hope I'm answering this the right way for you.
Have you noticed that you’ve been moving more slowly than usual, or that you can’t sit still and feel restless?

Well... I really hate to admit this one, because I've always prided myself on pulling my weight. I don't want you to think I'm just slacking off on purpose. But... yes, the guys at the job have actually started pointing it out to me. 

Sometimes I guess I'm just moving so slow... it literally feels like my boots are full of wet cement. They'll see me taking forever just to bend down and pick up a single board. And then, other times, it's the exact opposite, but just as bad. I get... I don't know, I just get stuck pacing around the shop, rubbing my hands together, and I'm not actually getting anything useful done at all. 

I feel terrible about it because I know it's frustrating for the crew, and I'm really trying my best to just snap out of it and be productive again. I know I just need to focus better. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it clearly enough for your notes.
Have you ever felt so overwhelmed or hopeless that you've thought about hurting yourself or that life isn't worth living?

Well... this is a really hard one to talk about, and I hope you don't think less of me for saying it. I know I have a lot to be thankful for, and I really don't want to sound ungrateful for my life or my family. But... yes, things have gotten pretty dark lately.

I haven't made any plans to hurt myself or anything like that, I promise. It's just... sometimes, when I'm feeling really low, I've had these thoughts that maybe... maybe it would just be easier if I went to sleep and didn't wake up. And, well, I catch myself thinking that my family might actually be better off without me dragging them down. 

It really scares me when my mind goes there, because I love them so much and I know I should be stronger than this. I try to push those thoughts away as soon as they pop up. I know it's a terrible way to think, and I'm so sorry if that's upsetting to hear. I just want to be completely honest with you so you can help me. Is it okay that I shared that with you? I hope I didn't say the wrong thing.
